title: Template Refs & Composition API in Depth

questions.prompt: When is a template ref populated with its DOM element?

options.text: After the component mounts (e.g. in onMounted)

questions.explanation: Template refs are null during setup and are filled once the element is mounted, so you access them in onMounted or later.

questions.prompt: How does a <script setup> child let a parent call one of its methods via a ref?

options.text: It's automatic — all methods are public
The child declares the method with defineExpose

questions.explanation: <script setup> components are closed by default; defineExpose declares which properties/methods are visible to a parent's component ref.

questions.prompt: You change state and immediately need to read the updated DOM. What do you await?
questions.explanation: Vue batches DOM updates; awaiting nextTick() resolves after those updates are applied, so the DOM reflects your latest state.

questions.prompt: To destructure a reactive object without losing reactivity, wrap it with to______. (complete the word)
questions.explanation: toRefs converts each property of a reactive object into a linked ref, so destructured values stay reactive.

questions.prompt: What does toValue(x) do that unref(x) does not?

options.text: It also calls x if x is a getter function, not just unwrapping a ref

questions.explanation: unref returns x.value for a ref (else x). toValue additionally invokes x when it's a getter function — ideal for MaybeRefOrGetter inputs in composables.

questions.prompt: If you put ref="item" on an element inside a v-for, what does the ref hold?

options.text: An array of the elements, in list order

questions.explanation: A ref used inside v-for collects the rendered elements into an array whose order matches the list.
